rubric.result: The objective promises two things and the diff produces both. (a) 'POST /review-plan falls to the 404 net': the `app.post(ReviewPlanRoute.PATH, ...)` and `app.all(ReviewPlanRoute.PATH, ReviewPlanRoute.refuseOtherMethods)` pair leaves `ApiServer.#route()` (api-server.ts now goes from the ImplementPlanRoute `app.all` straight to `PlanEventsRoute`), so the path reaches `app.use(Failures.nothingMatched)`, which is `Answer.refuse(response, 404, 'not-found', 'not found')` at api-server.ts:94. (b) 'the route and the action behind it are gone from the backend': `backend/src/infrastructure/review-plan-route.ts` (262 lines) and `backend/src/application/actions/ask-plan-changes.ts` (36 lines) are deleted files in the diff, and grepping the worktree for `ReviewPlanRoute`, `AskPlanChanges` and `askPlanChanges` across `backend/src` and `backend/__tests__` returns nothing but the surviving `/review-plan` string literals of the two new tests and `backend/API.md` (which Task 1 does not own). Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names `it('review_plan_is_no_longer_routed_and_falls_to_the_last_net')` in api-server.test.ts and fixes the assertion: 'a POST /review-plan with a well-formed body answers 404 and { code: not-found, detail: not found }'. The test in the diff (api-server.test.ts:1326-1333) posts `RunningApi.REVIEW_BODY` = `{"issue":7,"repo":"owner/name","changes":"parte la tarea 2"}` — a well-formed body for the retired contract — to `/review-plan` and asserts `expect(response.status).toBe(404)` and `expect(await response.text()).toBe('{"code":"not-found","detail":"not found"}')`. Same input, same assertion, same expected value as the phrase the plan wrote; asserting on the literal body text rather than the parsed object is stricter, not weaker.

The brief carries no `Contract` or `Call site` block; it carries one `Current state (backend/src/infrastructure/api-server.ts, lines 188-195)` block quoting the eight lines to remove — the `app.post` with its four middlewares and `ReviewPlanRoute.handledBy(this.askPlanChanges!, this.activePlans!)`, plus the `app.all`. The diff removes exactly those eight lines and nothing adjacent: `StartPlanRoute`, `ImplementPlanRoute`, `PlanEventsRoute`, `ActivePlansRoute`, `ImplementProgressRoute`, `ImplementHistoryRoute` and `ExternalToolsRoute` keep their `app.post`/`app.get` + `app.all` pairs unchanged, and `ImplementPlanRoute.handledBy` keeps its seven arguments (its trimming is Task 3's). No symbol the brief names is stated differently by the diff.

Every row this diff bears on is implemented with the stated value. 'What "no longer routed" means' — both the `app.post` and the `app.all` leave `#route()`, the answer is 404 `{"code":"not-found","detail":"not found"}`, and no 405 and no dedicated refusal survive (`ReviewPlanRoute.refuseOtherMethods` and `ReviewCollapse` go with the deleted module). (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: nothing added returns or consumes a map; the only added expressions are two HTTP assertions and the shortened literal array of a test's own inventory. (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: no error type is added; `ReviewCollapse` and its `plan-changes-not-asked` code leave with the module, and no replacement is named for a module or a location.

Every `-` line that touches an assertion, a case or a test traces to a sentence of the task. The two whole files deleted — `review-plan-route.test.ts` (297 lines) and `ask-plan-changes.test.ts` (64 lines) — are named verbatim in `**Tests:**` ('Removed: … and the files review-plan-route.test.ts and ask-plan-changes.test.ts') and in the §2 row 'Which modules are deleted, not deprecated'. `review_plan_turns_away_a_foreign_browser_origin`, whose body carried `expect(askPlanChanges.execute).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`, is named in `**Tests:**` as removed. `review_plan_is_mounted_in_the_real_process_and_not_only_in_the_test_server` is named as removed and its replacement `review_plan_is_no_longer_mounted_in_the_real_process` as added; the assertion flips from 400/`no-live-planning-session` to 404/`not-found`, which is the `**Objective:**` itself, not a relaxation. In refusal-codes.test.ts the `-` lines remove retired *inputs* (`ReviewRequestOutcome`, `ReviewCollapse.CODE`) rather than assertions, and the three `ImplementRequestOutcome` entries dropped from `SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES` make `expect(repeated.sort()).toEqual([...CODES].sort())` stricter, since those codes must now *not* repeat — the §2 row spells that list out. The four `-      askPlanChanges: null,` lines in the route tests are object-literal wiring, not assertions, and the brief accounts for them ('each builds a whole ApiServer object literal naming askPlanChanges … each loses that one line and nothing else'). No pre-existing test ended up asserting less without a sentence asking for it.

The promised 404 is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. It comes from `Failures.nothingMatched` in `backend/src/infrastructure/api-server.ts:94`, reached because `#route()` no longer registers `/review-plan` — and it is reachable only because the production module `review-plan-route.ts` and its wiring are gone. Neither new test hard-codes the behaviour: `review_plan_is_no_longer_routed_and_falls_to_the_last_net` starts a real `ApiServer` on port 0 with no `askPlanChanges` double at all and reads the wire body over `fetch`, and `review_plan_is_no_longer_mounted_in_the_real_process` spawns the actual `ct-api.ts` entrypoint as a child process and asks it over HTTP, so the assertion passes only if the real process really stopped mounting the path. Restore the two `app.post`/`app.all` lines and both tests go red.

Every line of the diff traces to a sentence of the task, and nothing `### Out of scope` names by name is touched. Inside the thirteen declared files: api-server.ts and ct-api.ts lose exactly what the §2 row 'What goes with the route in Task 1' lists — `ct-api.ts` keeps `ReviewPlan`, `ReadChangesAsked`, `reviews`, `pullRequestReviews` and `MemoryReviewLog`, which belong to Tasks 3 and 4; api-server.ts keeps the `ReviewInFlightValue` import, the `reviews` collaborator and the seven-argument `ImplementPlanRoute.handledBy`, likewise later tasks. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along — the only edits beyond the deletions are the four one-line literal trims, the two test rewrites and the refusal-codes inventory, each named in the brief. There is no plan hunk in this diff: the plan's amendments (commits b341121 and c55a8e2) predate the run, so there is no amendment for me to justify here.

Two tests are added by the `+` lines, and both hold the three properties. `review_plan_is_no_longer_routed_and_falls_to_the_last_net` (api-server.test.ts:1326): deterministic — no clock, no randomness, no network beyond loopback, no sleep; isolated — `RunningApi.listening()` binds port 0 and the file's `afterEach(async () => { await RunningApi.stopAll() })` stops every server it started, and the test takes nothing from the order of the file; verifies real behaviour — the assertion is on the status and the literal wire body a real server returns, with no double in the arrange at all, so reverting the two production lines turns it red. `review_plan_is_no_longer_mounted_in_the_real_process` (ct-api-real-process.test.ts:436): deterministic — `CT_API_PORT: '0'`, a spawn whose port is read off the child's first stdout line with a 30s reject rather than a sleep; isolated — its own child process, killed by `afterEach(() => { Entrypoint.killAll() })`, and it writes nothing outside the temporary roots the file's other fixtures own; verifies real behaviour — it asks the real entrypoint over HTTP and reads `code` off the parsed answer. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` as this item requires; nothing in it or in the `testing-anti-patterns.md` it names is contradicted — both tests exercise real code with no mocks, no production class gained a test-only method, and no assertion is on a mock's call count. The one thing its 'Minimal' row could be read against — the `and` in `review_plan_is_no_longer_routed_and_falls_to_the_last_net` — is the name the plan wrote literally in its `**TDD:**` line and joins one behaviour's two halves rather than two behaviours, so it is not reported.
